applicable_when: The kernel launches 1715 CTAs of 128 threads each on a 132-SM H200, yielding only 0.81 waves. Most SMs finish their single block and sit idle for the tail. The IMC stall (32.4% of all stall cycles) is caused by the strided index expression x0 + 528*x1 — each CTA re-fetches these constants from the constant cache. Increasing XBLOCK from 128 to 1024 or 2048 reduces the CTA count from 1715 to ~214 or ~108, which: (1) fills fewer waves more completely, (2) amortizes per-CTA constant-cache overhead across more work per block, and (3) allows the compiler to unroll/vectorize the inner loop more aggressively. Adding @triton.autotune lets the runtime pick the best tile size across {512, 1024, 2048} with varying num_warps.

applicable_when: The kernel performs a scatter-store: reads from contiguous flat input (in_ptr0 + x2, stride=1) but writes to strided output (out_ptr0 + x0 + 528*x1) where x0=xindex%112 and x1=xindex//112. With XBLOCK=128, consecutive threads in a warp write to addresses separated by 528 floats (2112 bytes), causing fully non-coalesced stores. This is the root cause of the 51% L1TEX scoreboard stalls. Additionally, 1715 CTAs on 132 SMs = 0.81 waves (SOLBottleneck). The 32% IMC stall arises from too many small CTAs. Prior @triton.autotune + XBLOCK attempts all failed correctness (3 iterations). The correct fix is a 2D grid: rows x cols, making stores coalesced within each warp.
